# Glasgow four-layer routing

The saved board has **zero unconnected items and zero unexcluded errors** in KiCad 10.0.8. A fresh zone fill gives the same result. The board has 3,381 straight track segments, 672 through vias and 12 filled zones. All 272 footprint identities, positions, rotations, sides and lock states match the input, as do all 1,149 physical pads, their geometry, drills and net assignments.

## Fabrication

The order package contains the four copper layers, outline, masks, legends, paste layers, plated and nonplated drill files, Gerber job file, IPC-D-356 test netlist and fabrication instructions. The finished profile is 80 × 49 mm. Keep the KiCad project and custom rules beside the board when regenerating artwork.

**Quote filled, planarized, copper-capped vias and controlled impedance.** Forty routing-via centres lie inside SMD lands. The package calls for IPC-4761 Type VII treatment on all 672 routing vias and the 29 plated thermal holes in the exposed pads of U1, U8 and U36. The fabrication instructions identify these by drill tool and hit count. Connector shell slots and component holes stay open. The smallest via is 0.40 mm land / 0.20 mm finished drill. The minimum routed line is 0.15 mm, and the class clearance is 0.1499 mm. The fixed SW1 pad 3 has 0.17 mm nominal copper-to-profile clearance. Confirm those capabilities when ordering.

| Layer | Copper use |
| --- | --- |
| F.Cu | USB and crystal paths, seven FPGA expansion pairs, digital signals, local supply connections and ground fill |
| In1.Cu | Main ground reference. Its fill forms one connected polygon. About 82 mm of local tracks cross this layer, mainly around congested digital escapes. |
| In2.Cu | General 3.3 V distribution, separate 1.2 V, protected 5 V and adjustable VIOA/VIOB regions, ground behind the rear expansion routes and USB connector, and about 390 mm of track |
| B.Cu | Six expansion pairs, local load and sense paths, general signals and ground fill |

The nominal 1.60 mm FR-4 build has 35 µm copper on each layer, 0.215 mm outer dielectrics, a 1.010 mm core, 10 µm mask per face and ENIG finish. With nominal dielectric constant 4.5, an idealized two-dimensional cross-section calculation gave approximately 90 Ω differential for USB and 100 Ω for the expansion pairs. The targets apply to the coupled runs. The fabricator needs to confirm them with its production materials, etch compensation and coupon.

## Routing decisions

- **USB and crystal.** The main J1 A6/A7 path stays on F.Cu, passes through the protection-device lands at U15 and reaches the FX2 at U1. D+ is 9.967 mm and D− is 10.708 mm, a 0.741 mm difference, with zero signal-layer changes on that path. The reversible connector contacts and rear test lands create short branches near J1. A ground via beside TP14 joins the local rear return to the ground system. The main USB geometry is 0.30 mm width / 0.20 mm gap. The 24 MHz crystal nets stay on the front, with 5.39 mm and 7.07 mm of copper and zero vias.
- **Expansion.** All thirteen U30–J5 Z pairs run together through the ordered fanout. Seven stay on top. Each conductor of the other six uses two vias, one near the FPGA and one near J5. The coupled runs use 0.22 mm width / 0.18 mm gap, with 0.15 mm escapes. The largest final conductor-length difference is 1.025 mm on Z10. Both differential classes have a 0.55 mm outer-layer ground-pour setback. The In2 ground region follows the rear pairs. A centreline sample found about 222 mm of their 263 mm of combined rear trace directly over ground. The rest includes connector and BGA escapes, track clearances and antipads.
- **Digital interface.** Rerouted CLKREF into the digital section after the first complete route exceeded 110 mm. Final total copper is 26.06 mm on CLKREF and 25.26 mm on CLKIF, including their test-point branches. The FX2–FPGA D0–D7 nets span 12.25–38.28 mm. D0 takes the longest detour. Timing margin and full-channel signal integrity have not been bench verified.
- **Power and measurement.** The protected 5 V trunk has an inboard path around the lower-right mounting hole. The two adjustable I/O banks have independent supply copper and local connections at the translators. The mirrored regulator/shunt sections use 0.48–0.55 mm load copper and separate sense pickoffs from the populated 0.15 Ω shunts to the monitor filters. Feedback stays close to the regulators. Where signal tracks or drill clearances divide a supply pour, explicit traces and vias join its connected sections. Local ground-plane cuts and narrow supply bridges are compromises of the fixed placement. DC drop under maximum simultaneous bank load has not been measured.

## Checks and inherited findings

- Ran KiCad DRC on the saved board and again with a fresh fill. No open connections, shorts, clearance errors, dangling tracks, dangling vias or thermal-relief violations were reported. The 414 warnings match the original board by type, description and implicated object IDs. They consist of 174 footprint-library mismatches, 77 footprint-library issues, 68 courtyard overlaps, 32 text-height warnings, 31 silkscreen overlaps, 26 silkscreen-to-mask clips and six silkscreen-to-edge clips. Some close courtyards involve actual components, including the headers and nearby passives. Assembly fit remains a separate check.
- Four inherited component-type errors have individual documented exclusions. U1, U8 and U36 are surface-mount packages with plated thermal holes. J1 has surface-mount contacts and plated shell anchors. The rule severity settings are the same as the input project. The edge rule permits the existing switch land while requiring 0.25 mm on tracks, vias and zones. A front-layer rule gives J4 pin 1 a solid ground connection where a thermal could only form one spoke.
- Schematic parity reproduces the original 421 warnings. These include field and net-name differences, extra and duplicate graphical footprints, and the C90/C91 PCB value fields, whose schematic values are 1 nF. A separate bidirectional comparison of reference and pad numbers against the exported schematic verified identical electrical grouping for all 1,063 connected pin numbers on all 251 logical nets. There are 59 alternate net names.
- The stricter bt check found current fills, zero split nets and zero additional copper findings. Its overall result is CHECK FAILED because it promotes the 68 fixed courtyard overlaps to errors and includes the four footprint-type exclusions. KiCad plotted all four copper layers, both masks, legends and paste layers, and the closed outline. Independent plated and nonplated drill files and the test netlist exported successfully.
